United had hoped to sell Manuel Ugarte and Zirkzee this summer and were in the market for buyers for Marcus Rashford, but the window could close with all three staying put. Ugarte’s serious knee injury put paid to the Uruguay midfielder leaving and Rashford has been reintergrated in the squad after Barcelona opted against taking up an option to sign him permanently.

Benfica are in talks about loaning Argentina Under-23 forward Claudio Echeverri from Manchester City, It’s likely to be a season long loan with an option to buy if finalised.

Fabio Vieira has completed his move from Arsenal to Hamburg, in a deal believed to be worth about £9m. The Portuguese midfielder has never cut it in the Premier League and it is no surprise that Arsenal have cashed in. They paid more than £30m to sign him from Porto in 2022 but he has never come close to justifying the fee. In truth, it’s one of their worst transfers under Mikel Arteta.

𝑾𝑬𝑳𝑪𝑶𝑴𝑬 𝑩𝑨𝑪𝑲, Fabio! 😍🔥Der 26-jährige Spielmacher wechselt nun fest vom FC Arsenal zu uns und unterschreibt einen langfristigen Vertrag. Die Rückennummer für die Saison 2026/27 steht noch nicht fest. ✍️🗣️ „Ich bin sehr glücklich, wieder hier zu sein. Ich habe… pic.twitter.com/P8YFRXFvgy

Southampton forward Cameron Archer is on course to sign for Auxerre on a season-long loan.

Archer has been a target for a number of Championship clubs this summer but a deal has been problematic because of his £35,000-a-week wages.

It is understood Southampton have been demanding that his salary be paid in full, which has scared off interested clubs in the second tier.

Chelsea will hold off sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City until they are confident of making at least one signing of their own.

Telegraph Sport understands that Chelsea have already rejected one proposal from City for Fernández during club-to-club talks and are demanding a fee and payment terms that are favourable to them.

Chelsea also have three separate targets of their own as potential deadline signings – Lamine Camara, Manu Kone and one mystery target from the Premier League.

Monaco have already rejected a £38.5m bid from Chelsea for Camara. Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini wants to keep Kone, although negotiations continue. And there is a third target from the Premier League, who is not believed to be Morgan Gibbs-White.

Chelsea must make significant progress on one of their targets before they will sanction Fernández’s sale – and City must make another bid that is more favourable to the club.

Monaco have rejected an opening €45m bid from Chelsea for midfielder Lamine Camara. It now remains to be seen if the club increase that offer.

Sunderland have been trying to sign a winger all summer and it appears that they have finally got their man in Lyon’s Malick Fofana.

Arsenal had been linked with a move for the 21-year old Belgium international.

Announcing Ansah! ✍️🔗 https://t.co/gweqxOt7aR pic.twitter.com/geZR60ZaTG

The Argentina forward missed three training sessions last week and was not included in Diego Simeone’s squad that travelled to Sevilla last weekend.

Nueva sesión de trabajo del Atleti en Majadahonda esta mañana. Julián Alvarez entrenando con normalidad con el resto del grupo. Objetivo, intentar estar en la lista de convocados para el partido ante el Athletic. Sorloth será baja por lesión. Imagen: @jsancris_ #ClubUria pic.twitter.com/IXAWX7mwrJ

Plenty of chatter about the future of Roma midfielder Manu Koné, who is linked with a move to Chelsea. The France international would be a strong acquisition for Xabi Alonso, but could his potential signing precede an Enzo Fernández exit? All will be revealed in due course...

Of Koné, former France manager Didier Deschamps said: “He’s very effective at winning the ball back, but he shouldn’t be limited to that role of defensive midfielder, because he also makes a difference in his use of the ball.”

Austria centre-back David Affengruber has emerged as potential deadline-day deal for Fulham as they look to bolster Alvaro Arbeloa’s defence.

The Elche player has been in La Liga for two years playing regularly and fits the data model at Craven Cottage.

Fulham are also trying deals for Real Madrid’s Manuel Angel and Eintracht Frankfurt’s Hugo Larsson as midfield options.

Sunderland are expected to complete the signing of centre-back Kevin Danso from Tottenham Hotspur with the player travelling to Wearside last night for the first part of his medical.

The Austria international will initially join on loan with an obligation to make the move permanent for £25m next year.

Danso had made it clear he wanted to leave Tottenham this summer in search of regular first-team football.

Eintracht Frankfurt are in talks with Nottingham Forest over another loan move for forward Arnaud Kalimuendo.

Frankfurt signed the Frenchman on loan in January and are negotiating a return for Forest’s £26m signing from Rennes.

Oliver Glasner, Forest’s head coach, had been intent on keeping Kalimuendo but it is understood Frankfurt’s strong interest has altered the club’s thinking.

Morato, the centre-back, is expected to join West Ham United on loan.

Forest are exploring potential signings but are determined to stay calm and only pursue deals that make financial sense. A winger and a No 6 are the two priority targets if there are deals to be done.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

“I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”

Richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

“If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

“But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”

It will be good news for Arsenal if Folarin Balogun completes his £40m move to Everton today. When Arsenal sold Balogun to Monaco in 2023, they negotiated a sell-on clause of 17.5 per cent. According to my maths, that means Arsenal will get £7m from this transfer. Not to be sniffed at!

Hull City are close to agreeing a fee of around £7.5m for Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas.

The Wales international has been a long-term target for Hull and negotiations are now approaching a conclusion.

Thomas has been pushing a move through and is expected to leave Stoke after one full season.

As has become the norm this summer Acun Ilicali has posted a cryptic message on X, which has prompted speculation among Hull City fans. The club has been linked with Everton holding midfielder Tim Iroegbunam.

Will Barcola hit the ground running at Anfield? The France winger registered 20 goal contributions in 49 games for Paris St-Germain last season.

A warm welcome from the skipper 😍 pic.twitter.com/95EAqUjYBn

The La Masia graduate secures a permanent move to Germany. Who knows how his career in England would have panned out had Chelsea not recalled him 25 days into his Sunderland loan at the beginning of last season...

Marc Guiu has completed a permanent transfer to Bundesliga side RB Leipzig. Everyone at Chelsea would like to thank Marc for his efforts during his time at the club and wish him every success as he begins the next chapter of his career with RB Leipzig.

What a couple of weeks it has been for Robert Sanchez. He came into this season as Chelsea’s No 1, but after a difficult start to the campaign and Emi Martinez’s arrival, reports suggest he could be moving away from Stamford Bridge on loan. Cesc Fabregas’s Como appears the probable destination.

Trevoh Chalobah, who left Chelsea for Como last month, has taken to his “secondary” Instagram account to post the following picture...

Meanwhile, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, striker flop Nick Woltemade is moving to Juventus on a season-long loan. The club’s record signing from as year ago at £64m is moving to Turin for a £3.5m loan fee with the Serie A squad covering the full cost of his wages.

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

In an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

In terms of outgoings, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy are expected to stay at the club despite interest from Nottingham Forest and Besiktas. Young striker Sean Neave will be allowed to leave on loan. The 19-year-old has offers from clubs in the Championship and League One but Newcastle want him to go somewhere he has the best chance of getting regular first-team football.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

Given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

A post shared by Ligue 1 McDonald's (@ligue1mcdonalds)

The Leeds wide man has a medical booked with Fiorentina today. He made a handful of appearances for Daniel Farke’s side during pre-season but has not featured since the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

✈️ L'arrivo di Gnonto a Firenze ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/nEFngsyxQP

Very unlikely that Liverpool will be doing any major incoming business but there may yet be some departures. Jayden Danns, who broke through three years ago and played in the 2024 League Cup final defeat of Chelsea, is attracting interest from clubs in Europe, who want to take him on loan. Danns, a promising striker, has had injury issues and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Fax machines are whirring as the clock continues to tick towards the transfer deadline, but who does your club need to sign? Let us know in the comments below!

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

Nottingham Forest can confirm Omari Hutchinson has joined AC Milan on a season-long loan deal, with the Italian club holding an option to make the transfer permanent.Everyone at Nottingham Forest wishes Omari all the best for his time in Italy. pic.twitter.com/fSv1uNGh2Y

Fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#2052. Newcastle United v Arsenal preview ahead of this St James’ Park match

Welcome to the Newcastle United v Arsenal preview

Saturday 21st November and a 5.30pm kick-off.

Newcastle United host Arsenal on Saturday  looking to get a stop-start season back on track against the table-topping champions.

The Toon have picked up a disappointing five points from five home league matches so far this season having lost the last two without scoring a goal.

Saturday represents a huge chance to put that right against an Arsenal side who haven’t got the best of recent records on Tyneside.

A late kick-off allows some extra time in various Tyneside hostelries which usually contributes to a cracking atmosphere. Lets hope Toon fans will be loud, proud and celebrating come full-time .

Newcastle have won two, drawn one and lost three of their past six league matches. Wins have come over Hull City and Crystal Palace whilst we’ve drawn with Fulham. Frustratingly, we’ve also suffered deserved defeats against Coventry, Villa and Everton. We’ve scored six goals in these games and conceded eight. The seven points gained has us languishing in a disappointing twelfth league position but a win could fire us up the table.

Arsenal are the form team in the league right now having won five in a row. Since losing to Brighton in September, they’ve gone on to beat Leeds, Everton, Forest, Liverpool and Hull. They’ve conceded four goals in these matches and scored seven, they’ve kept four clean sheets in the row. They are currently five points clear at the top of the table and will be hoping to have extended that lead come Saturday night.

Newcastle travelled to Fulham before the international break hoping to achieve their fourth straight success in the capital after wins over Spurs, Millwall and Crystal Palace. United started brightly with Harvey Barnes forcing two good saves before Dan Burn thought he’d given us the lead only for his effort to be ruled out for a foul in the build-up from Wissa. At the other end, Hornicek was in fine form making a string of good saves as the sides went into the half-time break goalless. The second half continued in a similar vein with both sides sensing they could win and when the breakthrough was finally made, it was the Toon fans celebrating. Jacob Murphy picked up the ball and beat two men before unleashing an incredible strike into the top corner with just ten minutes to play. Unfortunately the party in the away end was to be very short-lived indeed as just a few minutes later, Fulham equalised to set up a grandstand finish where both teams had chances to grab a late winner. Lewis Hall was played in on goal on the stroke of ninety minutes only to see his weak effort easily stopped before Hornicek pulled off an incredible save to salvage a point for the Toon who had to be content with a 1-1 draw.

Arsenal hosted Hull City in their last match and were frustrated by the Tigers for much of the ninety minutes. They scored late on to seal a 1-0 victory and had cause for further celebration when Man City lost a few hours later. The champions are determined to maintain their grip on the trophy.

-Newcastle have won four of their last six home games against the Gunners in all competitions.

-NUFC have found the net in their last four home matches against Arsenal.

-The Toon have beaten Arsenal at home on nine Premier League occasions.

Graeme Souness was enduring a rotten start to the 05/06 season when Arsenal visited St James’ Park in December. The Toon had failed to score in their opening five matches of the campaign but the arrival of Michael Owen seemed to have brought about a change in fortunes with five wins and two draws in our next ten games. Despite this, Souness was on borrowed time and this match against the Gunners would end up being one of the highlights of his ill-fated reign as manager. Newcastle spent most of the first half on the back foot and were grateful to Shay Given for a number of saves (one in particular even being applauded from Arsenal striker Thierry Henry!) but the Toon were getting stuck in and this physical approach was rattling the Reds who weren’t used to not having their own way.

At the start of the second half, the match descended into a real blood and thunder encounter which proved too much for Arsenal midfielder Gilberto Silva who was sent off for two bookable offences. Arsenal were then furious that an Alan Shearer foul on Sol Campbell wasn’t punished with a card and decided to fight fire with fire leading to a disgraceful assault on Scott Parker from the Arsenal ‘keeper that left our man short of a couple of teeth! Incredibly Parker played on with a mouth full of cotton wool as he bravely battled for every ball until another Arsenal foul left him sprawled out on the turf signalling to be subbed off. By now, Newcastle really had the bit between their teeth (if Scott Parker can pardon the expression!) and the crowd could sense a goal was coming.

With just nine minutes left, Shearer’s physicality allowed him to hold the ball up on the edge of the area and lay it off to Solano who fired home a spectacular effort at the Leazes End to spark wild and ecstatic celebrations. Not for the first (or last) time, Arsenal proved they don’t like it up ‘em at St James’ and Febregas threw a strop when unwisely attempting to start a fight with Alan Shearer before the match had even restarted. As the away side huffed and puffed looking for an equaliser, it became apparent that this would be Newcastle’s day and Micheal Owen even had a chance to double the lead near the end that unfortunately he couldn’t take. The final whistle brought an outpouring of joy and relief as the Toon Army celebrated a Merry Christmas victory. A week later, we’d go to West Ham and a Micheal Owen hat-trick was the cornerstone of a brilliant 4-2 win. If Graeme Souness felt his luck was turning however then he had another thing coming. Owen would break his foot a week later and Souness was given the sack having achieved just one point from the next six matches. Glenn Roeder would come in and steady the ship with a tremendous end to a tumultuous season but that’s a story for another day. Newcastle 1-0 Arsenal.

Malcolm Macdonald – Some of our older readers will have fond memories of this legendary number nine. ‘Supermac’, as he was affectionately known by fans, kick-started his Toon career with a hat-trick in his first home match against Liverpool. What was to follow has gone down in Toon Army folklore! Scoring one hundred and twenty-one goals in just two hundred and twenty-seven appearances has him up there with the best of the best in NUFC history. Perhaps his finest hour came in the 1974 FA Cup Semi-Final when he scored two second half goals to defeat Burnley 2-0 at Hillsborough and send United to their first FA Cup final for nineteen years. Unfortunately, he couldn’t repeat this feat at Wembley as a tame performance was punished by a 3-0 defeat to a Kevin Keegan inspired Liverpool. There was uproar when he was sold to Arsenal for a third of a million pounds in 1976. He went on to score forty-two goals in eighty-four league games for the Gunners.

Andy Cole began his career by playing one league game for Arsenal before being loaned to Fulham and then sold to Bristol City. Kevin Keegan broke the club’s transfer record by splashing out £1.75 million for the striker in 1993. This is a number nine who’s record stands up to anyone else’s – a whopping sixty-eight goals in eighty-four matches before being controversially sold to Man United in January 1995 for a British record transfer fee. Some fans were so angry at the sale that they turned up at the stadium demanding answers which Keegan provided, famously standing on the steps to explain his decision. King Kev would go on to sign both Sir Les and Alan Shearer as the entertainers came ‘so close’ to being champions of England for the first time since 1927 and the debate still rages on about which of the three was the best number nine of NUFC’s Premier League era.

Sol Campbell was something of a legend at Arsenal having run down his contract at arch-rivals Tottenham to join the Gunners on a free transfer. He’d go on to win a number of trophies and even grabbed a goal in the 2006 Champions League final. He played a handful of games for NUFC in 2010 but it’s safe to say he was well past his best when donning the famous black and white.

Matthias Jaissle after a 1-1 draw away at Fulham: “A step in the right direction after the last performance. That’s something we can really build on.I think there were occasions also to win that game. Of course, the disallowed goal, a soft one, I would say. I see it differently then also a big chance at the end. Then you should go home with three points but one point and a performance is something we can work on. It’s now time to reflect and recharge also with a long season ahead of us, then pull out the things we need to improve and there are a couple of aspects, but today showed a clear direction in the right way so we can build on that. We did enough to win. We spoke clearly through the week and we saw that today, there was complete commitment and togetherness in all phases. The first 20 minutes there was a lack of confidence from last week but we grew through the game and that was excellent, something to build on.”

Mikel Arteta after a 1-0 win at home to Hull City:  “Not beautiful but effective. I’m delighted with the win because to go to the international break after winning is one of the best things for a coach or for a player. I think, regarding the performance, we were the better team. I think we had enough chances and situations to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren’t efficient enough to do that, and then we have to rely on generating volume, generating a lot of situations in and around the box until we are able to break them down.This is exactly how we won the game, and Martin, the way he scores, is not the most beautiful one but the most effective one, which is a simple shot and then following the next action, and that was enough today to win again.”

Newcastle United fans food bank will once again be collecting opposite the Gallowgate end and gratefully receiving food, money and toiletries for those in need. Of particular interest are non-perishable food and drink items (such as noodles, pasta, rice, canned food, soup, cereal, cordial, long life milk etc) as well as toiletries such as shower gel, shampoo, toothpaste and sanitary products. Please give whatever you can, any donation is very much appreciated.

For further info and/or to donate online go to Newcastle Foodbank

There can be no doubt that Newcastle have been poor recently despite showing some promising signs of improvement against Fulham last match. Games after an international break are notoriously difficult to predict. The bookies may be looking at this as something of a formality but we seem to do a lot better against the bigger sides and have a great recent record at home against the Gunners. I was thinking this may be a score draw but my confidence has been growing throughout the week so I’m going for a wildly-celebrated win followed by a few sore heads on Sunday morning. Newcastle 2-1 Arsenal.

#2051. Simple: Scott Parker’s secret weapon in West Ham reboot

West Ham return to action tomorrow with a home tie against visitors Preston North End – a team who sit rock bottom of the Championship but are not without their recent triumphs after turning over promotion-chasing Southampton just before the break. So West Ham need to be wary, despite their opponents’ lowly league table position.

With Scott Parker having enjoyed an unbroken two week training period during the break, West Ham fans will now surely get to see the ‘Parker XI’ rather than Nuno’s inherited lin-up with which he began the first two games of his West Ham tenure.

The first visible difference will surely be to see -shock, horror – players used in their correct positions: Nuno because infamous for using square pegs in round holes – Morato at left back being the case in point.

Morata’s days at left back are surely over

Despite being signed as a centre back and having played all but 33 of his last 177 games as such, Nuno insisted on using the 6’3 Brazilian – hardily the most mobile – as a left back who was frequently found to be out of position, often allowing wingers to get the better of him: Scott Parker hooked him at half time after a pretty inept left-back performance against Cardiff.

With centre back Maximilian Kilman suspended for tomorrow’s clash there should be no more Morato at left back – incredibly West Ham fans have never seen the loanee in his preferred specialist position until now. Ezra Mayers has already done enough to start at left back leaving Parker free to slot Morato into the role for which he was signed, alongside Mavropanos.

Square pegs into square holes: Scott Parker’s secret weapon in his West Ham reboot. Who’d have thought.

Listeners of The Mag Podcast will know there was a little Newcastle United theme going on to pass the time during the international break. Comparing a past season with the current one.

I’m going to do exactly the same, not with a season such as 2008-09. That’s too far in the past for me.

I’m going back to last (2025-26) season and comparing it with this 2026-27 season after 10 games.

The difference in the Premier League table between now and last season after 10 games. The difference? One place higher than last season, from 13th to 12th.

It had me wondering, is it going to be such a season again?

Last season wasn’t a remarkable one for Newcastle United and the fans.

It was a season with a lot of frustration and one that ended with a lot of players leaving the club at the close of the season.

Both Newcastle United seasons have 12 points after 10 games, though the goal difference is slightly worse this time, going from -1 to -3.

After 10 games Newcastle United have now scored three more goals than at this point last season BUT have also conceded five more.

This next game is against Arsenal, the reigning Champions and five points clear at the top, then it is second in the table Brighton.

It is then huge games against Man United and Sunderland games,

These next four matches could be pivotal when it comes to the morale of the players and whether we fall into a relegation battle, maybe even the future of Matthias Jaissle at St. James’ Park will be at risk.

What this season is going to bring is still a mystery but the early signs don’t look promising…

West Ham have, thankfully, avoided some of the problems which competing clubs have endured with huge swathes of first team players injured. Cardiff City struggled with eight players injured before the West Ham tie, but it didn’t stop the Bluebirds racing into a three goal lead and almost inflicting what would, in view of their first team being ‘decimated’, have been a humiliating defeat on their visitors.

By comparison, the Hammers have largely escaped such wholesale problems. Manor Solomon’s back problem and Kyle Walker Peters’ muscle issue seemed to be the main worries until sportwitness.co.uk revealed another squad injury that had been flying largely under the radar:

“West Ham United‘s Keiber Lamadrid went under the knife to resolve the physical problems that hampered his growth and development in England….During pre-season, he again suffered a knee injury in the friendly against 1. FC Magdeburg. There were concerns about a serious setback, but he returned to the pitch in August.

Lamadrid hasn’t featured for West Ham – now we know why

The player hasn’t made it to the match day squad since mid-September. Meridiano [news outlet] in Venezuela now states that this is because of fitness concerns, which have bothered him since moving to England.

Keiber Lamadrid has ‘put an end to the series of physical problems’ that stopped him from enjoying regular minutes with the Hammers. He did this by undergoing knee surgery.”

An interesting take on Lamadrid’s absence from match day squads.

It had been assumed that he was simply not impressing Nuno in training but the reveal that he’s been dealing with a long standing knee problem might well offer optimism that there’s a lot more to come from the young midfielder-slash-winger when he’s fully recuperated.

#2047. West Ham’s Home Advantage Problem Won’t Disappear With 60,000 Fans

Mark Noble has called on West Ham United supporters to help transform the London Stadium into an intimidating venue as Scott Parker prepares for his first home match in charge against Preston North End.

Speaking in an interview with the club’s official website, Noble praised the ‘extraordinary’ loyalty of West Ham fans following relegation and insisted that the club’s ambition remains an immediate return to the Premier League.

He also challenged supporters to make life uncomfortable for visiting teams, arguing that a crowd of 60,000 should give West Ham a significant advantage. But I think it’s important to point out that getting the fans onside and creating an intimidating atmosphere are probably two very different things.

There’s no doubt about it. When the London Stadium is loud, it is impressive, as anybody who attended that incredible night against Sevilla will testify.

But I do think it’s a long way from being intimidating.

For that to happen, I firmly believe supporters need to be close to the pitch.

Not just to cause opposition players discomfort, but to put pressure on referees and give West Ham the kind of home advantage that seems prevalent throughout the league.

The distance between the stands and the playing surface remains a fundamental problem, regardless of how many supporters are in attendance.

It’s something I’ve previously argued when discussing proposals to improve the stadium atmosphere.

Isolated tiers in the stadium and poor pitch proximity do little to help the atmosphere at the London Stadium

It was always my concern that relegation to the Championship would see visiting teams regard a trip to the London Stadium as a lovely day out in opulent surroundings. Opposition changing rooms are grand and palatial and their team coach can pull into the venue untroubled by home fans.

And our results in Stratford have certainly done little to disprove that theory. However, that doesn’t mean things can’t improve.

I genuinely believe that getting West Ham playing on the front foot will help eliminate some of the eerie silences we’ve heard so frequently at the London Stadium.

Noble wants supporters to see a team giving everything, and I think he’s absolutely right about that.

If Parker can produce an aggressive, attacking side that gives the crowd something to get excited about, the atmosphere should improve considerably.

But turning the London Stadium into a genuinely intimidating venue is another matter entirely.

And unfortunately, that’s a problem which can’t be solved simply by asking 60,000 people to make more noise.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

Looking at all of the top games on TV, the stadia are considerably worse than London Stadium for proximity of fans.

Maybe we just lack the pyrotechnics in the crowd. The mad grabbing and jostling of inferior beings next to us. The joy of trying to intimidate anyone. We also lack a car park to show off our loutish best.

Whatever you think of the stadium, great and intimidating atmospheres can be choreographed to deliver at kick off, but if the team start sluggishly and without energy then that atmosphere will quickly deflate.

We were famously close to the pitch at Upton Park and won nothing for decades.

Blaming the stadium is just a distraction from the fact that we’re not playing well; when Andy Carroll scored that overhead kick against Palace, no one near me said they didn’t appreciate because they weren’t closer to the pitch.

If the ‘quality’ of the stadium is so important, explain Spurs to me…

#2045. Revealed : Parker tears up the Nuno rule book in Rush Green revolution | West Ham News

Training ground videos from the Nuno Espírito Santo era usually featured someone else taking training sessions at Rush Green: The former Hammers boss was usually nowhere to be seen when the customary pre-game PR videos were released with one of his assistants running the session.

His preparation was also rumoured to be perfunctory with short, superficial pre-match meetings, none of which produced the results on the pitch that would have helped him keep his job and West Ham keep their Premier League status.

As revealed by Roshane Thomas, writing in the NYTimes:

“Under Nuno, training lacked intensity and largely focused on small-sided games and running. Pre-match team meetings are said to have lasted 10 minutes on average and lacked detail…

Nuno Espirito Santo’s training sessions criticised today in revealing new report

During the international break, he [Scott Parker] has focused on high-intensity training. It has been his preferred approach, rather than team bonding exercises away from their training hub in Rush Green.

The players, however, have noticed a big difference under Parker. With help from assistant coaches Mark Noble, Jonathan Hill, Steve Potts, Gerard Prenderville and Billy Lepine, Parker has prioritised working on pressing structure and shape with and without the ball.”

Which begs the question “Just what were the squad working on under Nuno”?

According to their new Manager, the changes he’s made have kicked in and there’s been a noticeable upturn. Which, lets face it, was long overdue, and after the new head coach’s first two games in charge was clearly, sorely needed.

“My general feeling is this is a group that are desperate to do well and work hard,” said Parker. “I’ve sensed that in the training sessions and what we’ve been doing. It’s still early days, I understand that, but there’s been some real improvement over the last two weeks”

We’ll all see for ourselves tomorrow when Preston North End visit: After his tough two-game baptism of fire, Parker got his two week break to prepare for a home tie against the bottom side. Which is as easy as it’s going to get this season.

#2043. Absolutely remarkable! Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 – Saturday 21 November 2026 5.30pm

If you ever wanted proof of how unpredictable football is, here is the ultimate proof.

Arsenal absolutely dominated the first half.

They looked very much like they were the reigning champions and league leaders by five points.

Newcastle United didn’t get a kick. Well, not a kick where it mattered.

Arsenal dominating the ball and territory, Newcastle just clearing the ball and it coming straight back at them.

Bruno Guimaraes had headed a close in header just wide and it felt like a goal was inevitable.

The visitors were breaking the half-hearted United press with ease and you really had to feel for Lewis Hall when the goal did come. He didn’t deal with a ball he should have, next thing Havertz with a very clever ball that Dedic wasn’t alive to and Eze giving Hornicek no chance.

Matthias Jaissle took decisive action for the second half, with Ramsey, Elanga and Livramento replacing Steur, Murphy and Dedic.

Inside four minutes Newcastle were level.

In almost the exact same part of the pitch, Odegaard made a far worse blunder than Hall had for their goal. Osula taking advantage to feed Barnes in the box and a great low finish.

It was then all suddenly Newcastle United pouring forward and the first half seemed like another match.

Just after the hour mark an excellent corner routine saw Hall cross from the right and Burn a free header, that caused chaos and Malick Thiaw on hand to smash it home from a yard out.

Var vainly tried to find a handball, then it was looking for an offside, before admitting defeat.

Somehow, somehow, Newcastle United were now ahead!

Newcastle didn’t sit back and continued to look for another goal, absolutely the right tactics. Rather than sit back.

Arteta making subs and Bruno Guimaraes trudging off as one of them.

The Arsenal equaliser was a great goal for them as they played it from back to front but Newcastle could have defended it better as Madueke cut inside. Plus Hornicek should have saved it, even though the shot went through a defender’s legs.

More than twenty minutes then played including nine minutes added time, with a pretty even closing period of the match, even though you naturally adopted the stance of you just know Arsenal are going to find a winner somehow…

Never in a million years did you see that second half coming after Arsenal had total control of the first.

Newcastle at last seeing a bit of luck going their way with that Odegaard mistake and suddenly that helped give confidence and momentum. Plus it helped that United brought on three mobile players all able to carry the ball and with a bit of pace.

No doubt the extremist Matthias Jaissle haters won’t want to give him any credit.

However, I think he was brave with his substitutions and I have a feeling that whatever 11 he had played in the first half, we would have seen Arsenal dominate the opening 45.

A hopeless first half and a second half that gives hope.

‘It’s not an idiom to call that a game of 2 halves. They looked lost for the first 45 and were lucky to be just a goal down. We were by far the better team in the 2nd half and should have probably finished the game off on multiple occasions.’

‘Excellent second half after a first in which we looked low on confidence and bereft of ideas.

Fair play to Jaissle who had seen enough and his triple substitution paid dividends, United taking the game to Arsenal and unlucky not to have won.’

‘Wow, terrible first half, brilliant second.

Atmosphere was flat considering the number one rat’s return but thanks to our players for finally realising that effort equals reward.’

‘First half, woeful. Arsenal simply a class apart and it didn’t stick for any of our players.

Ultimately, we’d only earn a point despite being worthy of more with that second half performance.

Arsenal had won nine of ten Premier League matches and that was just brilliant from Jaissle and these players who clearly are very much still playing for him.”

‘Some much much-needed signs of life as the champions are held on Bruno’s return to Tyneside.

Folklore denoting he was bound to get booed.

Sadly, it wasn’t quite enough for a win, yet we become the only side bar Brighton to get something off the Gunners so far this season.

Heading into this one I did wonder if a point would be considered a great outcome.

The players duly obliged amid some major talking points, not least the manager leaving £259m worth of signings on the bench, and a further £72m (Toure and Bamba) in the stands.

‘That’s a point more than I thought we’d get.

How come every game we play in the first half after a week’s training and pre match instructions still fresh in their ears, we are awful?

And then when the players play the game in front of them in the second half they suddenly improve despite / regardless of the half time talk from the Head Coach?

#2040. European hero still has a vital role to play as expectation rises ahead of Preston clash | West Ham News

West Ham’s veteran midfielder has been the subject of an honest interview in his home country on Czech radio coinciding with the release of his autobiography. One of the more revealing comments Tomas Soucek made concerns the pressure and the expectation of playing in front of a big audience – such as West Ham will undoubtedly face tomorrow as the season re-commences with a home tie at London Stadium in front of 60,000 expectant supporters.

Unlike several others, from his words it is clear that Soucek seems to thrive on the pressure and the weight of expectation upon him. As one of only a handful of medal winners still at the club from the 2023 campaign, Soucek’s experience should become a steadying influence in the dressing room even though he mostly starts games on the bench these days.

Handling the weight of expectation at London Stadium has been daunting at times

‘Tornado Tom’ reveals that, far from letting it get to him, he actually enjoys the weight of expectation and pressure :

“Yes, obviously I feel it, but I like the pressure. Because football is always up and down, you have so many wins and so many losses – and it’s up to you how you recover from all of it.

“And I love that. As you said, it’s the most watched league in the world. And West Ham’s fans are crazy – they’re the best in the league, and it’s such a historic club.

“From the first day until now, I think me and West Ham connection is as good as it could possibly be in all aspects.

“And, yes, the pressure is there, but I try to work with it – and that’s why we play football.” (englishradio.cz)

The pressure will be significantly eased with a clean sheet and three points tomorrow – whether Soucek now, 31 gets into the action or simply acts as a calming figure in the dressing room. He is one of those very rare characters in the West Ham team – a leader on and off the pitch – and in another era could have spent years as the club’s captain.

Mikel Arteta watched on as his Arsenal team dominated Newcastle United in the first half.

United fortunate to be only one down after the opening half.

Arsenal going six points clear but Brighton with a game in hand.

Mikel Arteta asked about Bruno Guimaraes making an emotional return to St James’ Park and how he thought he dealt with it: “Very good. We spoke about that before the game. Because inevitably, emotionally, you have so much going on, especially in the way that he feels connected to this club, having been the captain and everything that they did together. But I think he was very composed and he was very, very, very focused on what he had to do in the game. I think for the time that he was on the pitch he had a really good performance.”

Suggested to Mikel Arteta that a point at St James’ Park is usually a good result but that he won’t feel like that is the case tonight: “My feeling is that we lost two points today. We were exceptional in the first half, from the beginning to the end. The intensity, the level of aggression, the intensity that we put on the defensive aspects, the quality that we showed. Thee clarity to understand the jobs, the composure that we have with the ball, the aggressiveness that we have to attack the right spaces, we should have been two, three, or four up clearly. When you don’t do that then the opponent is going to try to react, we play at the same level but we still have to increase the level to cope with that. Then right at the beginning of the second half we aren’t at the races, we start to lose duels, we start to lose second balls, we give the ball away, really poor circulation goals against their press and their waves. When that happens, you give them belief. One thing is to give them belief, and another thing is to give them a goal. We give them a goal from a throw, that is obviously very, very, very disappointing. On top of that we give them a corner, we give them the best player that they have on the pitch on set-pieces free.”

Mikel Arteta on Newcastle United and the fans: “You have to give credit to Newcastle United as well for that period of time [when they were on top], the quality, the aggression, the conviction that they showed that they could get back in the game. The same with the stadium, which we know that when it comes to these evenings, they believe that they can do it, it’s another push. We have won football matches playing much worse than we have done here. But it is not enough because when the margins are so small, everything matters.”

#2034. West Ham’s Forgotten Wonderkid Lands Surprise Lifeline

Back in June, I wrote about a former West Ham academy graduate, a player once tipped for stardom after bursting onto the scene as a teenager. Many believed he had all the attributes needed to become a Premier League regular and potentially an England international. Sadly, football does not always follow the script, and Reece Oxford’s career gradually drifted away from the spotlight.

His move to German side Augsburg initially appeared to be the perfect opportunity to develop away from the intense scrutiny of English football. However, injuries and setbacks limited his impact, and after seven years with the Bundesliga club he departed in 2025 having made just 80 appearances.

Fast forward to this week and Oxford has been handed a fresh opportunity after Bromley announced the signing of the 27-year-old defender. The move could prove to be exactly what both player and club need.

There were high hopes for Reece oxford’s career: At still only 27 he has a chance of better times ahead

Karl Robinson, recently appointed manager of the Greater London  outfit, faces a significant challenge with Bromley currently sitting at the foot of League One. The Ravens will hope Oxford can provide a much-needed boost as the club look to climb the table.

Oxford has already spoken positively about the move, saying: “I’ve been here for a few weeks now getting my fitness levels up. Everyone has been great. All I can do is give something back to them now.”

Away from the media pressure that once followed his every step, this could be the ideal environment for Oxford to rebuild his confidence and rediscover the talent that once made him one of English football’s brightest prospects.

Everyone at C&H wishes him every success in the next chapter of his career.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

#2030. West Ham 1 – 1 Preston North End | Player ratings as Parker drops more points

West Ham again conceded in the first half and spent the rest of the game peppering Preston’s goal – four efforts hit the woodwork but to no avail until Mavropanos’ second half equaliser. A lack of clinical finishing cost Scott Parker’s side dear as the points were shared.

Encouraging early touches with his feet and a willingness to catch rather than punch initially inspired confidence. Failed to get his fists to a corner, the ball striking Piroe on the head and looping over Herrick to give Preston a simple goal to create their lead. A superb double save just before half-time kept West Ham in touch after Mayers’ poor header. Grew in stature in the second half, notably catching balls where Hermansen might have punched.

Good early interplay with Bowen down the right. Unlucky not to score when his effort crashed against the post immediately after Bowen had hit the woodwork. Replaced by Souček on 78 minutes.

Solid enough first half without really being tested. Slipped in to meet a deflected Engels cross and equalise in true Mavropanos style.

Looked far more comfortable in the combative centre-back role, without being seriously tested for pace. Met Solomon’s second half cross with a header that was blocked.

Solid enough first half until a dreadful defensive header gifted the ball back to Preston, with Herrick rescuing him through a superb double save. Booked after misjudging his control and pulling down an opponent. Replaced by Scarles on 78 minutes.

A great through ball released Piroe for West Ham’s first decent opportunity. Excellent work out wide, crossing with his weaker foot to allow Mavropanos to equalise. Lots of wide running in a much more advanced position than under Nuno. Looked better for it.

Making his first appearance of the season, showed little sign of rustiness. Should have equalised after a well-worked corner, curling into the side-netting. Looked increasingly at home sitting in front of the defence and moving remarkably quickly across the turf. Quick feet in the opposition box led to a shot poked agonisingly close, but just wide. A pretty good shift on his return; surprising he lasted until 90 minutes, when Magassa replaced him.

Should have taken a first-time shot with his right foot, but instead shifted onto his favoured left and scuffed the chance in the first half. Needs to produce more. Evidently Parker agrees as he was replaced by Castellanos on 57 minutes.

Struck the post with a right-footed effort as West Ham pressed for an equaliser. Had the beating of his full-back in the second half, making frequent runs down the right and crossing with his weaker foot. Several shots but lacked that killer punch – as did the whole attack.

Should have opened the scoring after ten minutes when sent through one-on-one by Engels, but the goalkeeper saved. Lots of trying and ‘nearlies’ but too little output. Booked on 82 minutes for a professional foul. Not enough from the striker.

A decent early effort from 25 yards went straight at the goalkeeper. Immediately after the restart, stepped inside and struck the bar with a brilliant curling right-footed shot. Replaced by Solomon on 57 minutes at which point West Ham’s pace and zip largely vanished. There’s a lesson in there…

On for Austbø, 57 minutes. One jinking run inside produced a cross met by Morato’s head, but the effort was blocked. Looked very right-footed and unable to beat defenders on the outside. West Ham were poorer for the substitution of Austbø and Solomon’s introduction.

On for Mukasa, 57 minutes. Fluffed his lines on 85 minutes, looping a back-post header over the bar.

On for Mayers, 78 minutes. One decent cross late on. Understandably rusty

On for Veltman, 78 minutes. Almost won it in the 94th minute with a back-post header tipped over by Preston’s goalkeeper.

#2029. West Ham 1 – 1 Preston | Final score, first impression as more points slip away

West Ham’s familiar profligacy in front of goal came back to haunt them, as did their propensity to go behind in the first half of games as the points were shared at London Stadium this afternoon.

From Preston’s first corner, the fanbase was understandably apprehensive, knowing West Ham’s weaknesses from dead balls earlier in the season. Again the curse struck, with Piroe heading the ball over his own oncoming goal keeper’s fists, the ball then looping onto the post and allowing a gentle tap-in for Preston to take the lead.

Herrick rallied well after conceding early

The wheels could have come off for West Ham’s young goal keeper at that point: However, all credit to Herrick. It would have been very easy for his confidence to crumble after that early combi-cock-up, but he rallied well and even appeared to be smiling as the game went on, with several catches and a couple of really good saves surely meaning the shirt is his for the time being.

West Ham hit the post four times during a frenetic period in the first half when their intensity was high, but it seemed as though the ball simply would not go between the posts.

Familiar problems surfaced in the second half as the pace dropped and West Ham ran out of ideas, notably after Austbø had been substituted. Manor Solomon, looking very one-footed, simply ran inside and passed square. Frustratingly, the game slowed in pace in the last twenty minutes with the Hammers looking devoid of new ideas just at the time when they should have been upping the tempo.

It is clear that there’s still a shortage of pace in this side and with a build up that got slower as the game went on, West Ham’s bench looked as if it desperately needed an injection of Antonio-like pace to scare opponents and perhaps take on a shot!

A disappointment for the West Ham supporters, who booed their team off in the now time-honoured tradition as another two points went west. Against the bottom side.

#2028. Scott Parker tells us there are positives – but talk is cheap | West Ham News

West Ham failed to overcome bottom side Preston North End in what was a desperately disappointing spectacle for West Ham fans who had been expecting so much more from their new manager’s first home game.

A scrappy first goal conceded came from pretty much Preston’s only attempt at goal, and then our visitors sat back in time-honoured tradition.  Four times the Hammers crashed the ball against the woodwork in a first half which showed plenty of promise, however the second half evaporated in familiar fashion, inexplicably, no sooner than Mavropanos crashed in the equaliser.

Just about every fan expected West Ham to go on and win the game convincingly – yet instead they huffed and puffed with endless ‘after you – no after you’ short, sideways passes as nobody took responsibility for making the killer pass or – heaven forbid- taking on the shot.

However, the West Ham manager will no doubt do his best, tomorrow maybe, to pull out positives, despite being ‘devastated‘ at the result:

Edson Álvarez, in his first game this season, El Machin was, surprisingly, up to speed pretty much immediately, sitting in front of the defence. He was everywhere: collecting, tidying up, harrying, attacking and breaking down opponents’ attacks. The late-tackling liability of last season was nowhere to be seen as he impressed and looks as if he has found himself a role for the coming weeks.

However, there’s a caveat: Remember this is the bottom side in the division who have just held us to draw. It will be intriguing to see if he copes against tougher opponents.

Edson Alvarez -Looked in control this afternoon – of his own discipline and of his midfield patch.

Finn Herrick: It can only have been unsettling, as the young keeper came to punch his first corner only to find a team mate’s glancing header got there first, looping the ball over his outstretched fists and allowing Preston to open the scoring against the run of play.

Credit to him, Herrick kept his cool and grew in stature as the game went on. He made an excellent double save after Mayers’ poor defensive header, and played well with the ball at his feet, combining Areola’s shot-stopping ability and Hermansen’s football skills.

However, positives aside, Parker has his work cut out simply to get this team’s work rate up. This time, they started quick and could have had three in the first half, even though there was a hesitancy and a lack of creation in front of goal.

Why it evaporated no sooner than the Hammers had equalised was a mystery. What should have become a barrage launched on Preston’s goal became a last thirty minutes of frustrating misfiring.

Just. Not. Good.Enough. Despite the bright points which Parker referenced in his post – match conference.

Just don’t blame West Ham’s newest manager for the failure of the last three to demand pacy, attacking football and recruiting so-called strikers who wouldn’t have made it into West Ham’s championships side of 2004/5 or 2011/12.

Can’t make a silk purse out of a sows ear. Especially not in two weeks.

#2027. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw
